system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: WINWORD.EXE opened C:\Users\maria.lopez\Downloads\Statement.docm, and shortly afterward launched PowerShell with no profile, a hidden-window flag, and an encoded command.
The encoded PowerShell command decodes to an expression that executes a string downloaded from raw.githubusercontent.com/harbor-dental-it/tools/main/u.ps1.
Proxy evidence records a successful request for that u.ps1 URL, and Sysmon attributes connections to the proxy to the same PowerShell process.
PowerShell then launched rundll32.exe with C:\Users\maria.lopez\AppData\Roaming\svchelper.dll,Init as its command line, an unusual execution chain consistent with malicious activity.
A separate PowerShell process ran as SYSTEM from a taskeng.exe parent using C:\Scripts\backup-check.ps1; that process also made an explicit-credentials logon using svc-claimsync.
The workstation made an SMB connection to FILE-HD-01 that the server logged as ANONYMOUS LOGON; the available SMB record does not show what, if anything, was accessed.
The earlier download of installer-60890.exe is recorded, but these records do not show that it was executed.

known_telemetry_limitations: The records do not include the contents or hash of Statement.docm, the downloaded u.ps1 script, or svchelper.dll.
The proxy records establish a request for u.ps1 but do not provide its response body; the process records do not establish what actions the script or DLL performed.
The available records do not establish whether the SYSTEM backup-check task or the SMB activity is related to the Word/PowerShell chain.
The records show process creation and network activity but do not provide a complete endpoint investigation or establish whether persistence, data access, or exfiltration occurred.
claims_not_established: That Statement.docm was delivered by an attacker or that a particular macro mechanism triggered PowerShell.
That the GitHub repository or downloaded script was controlled by an attacker; the URL alone does not establish ownership or legitimacy.
That svchelper.dll was successfully loaded, what it contained, or whether it created persistence.
That svc-claimsync credentials were misused or that the backup-check task was malicious.
That data was stolen, exfiltrated, or accessed over the SMB connection.
additional_evidence_needed: Acquire and analyze Statement.docm, u.ps1, svchelper.dll, and the temporary file, including hashes, timestamps, signatures, and content.
Collect PowerShell operational/script-block and AMSI logs, Office macro telemetry, and full endpoint process and file telemetry for WS-MLOPEZ-01.
Review scheduled-task configuration and history for the task that ran backup-check.ps1, and determine why it used svc-claimsync credentials on this workstation.
Obtain FILE-HD-01 SMB share and file-access auditing for the workstation connection, plus relevant DC and authentication logs.
Check whether the u.ps1 URL, downloaded content, or DLL appears on other endpoints or in related security alerts.
